- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.2), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect risk reversal or market recovery.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast 3–5 days post-spike.
- Forecast mean reversion bias: if 30-day forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment volatility >0.3 SD from mean triggers lag correction: delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days if sentiment is erratic or inconsistent.
- If sentiment history shows “reversal” (e.g., +0.6 → -0.4), model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: reduce forecast by 2–4% on day of reversal.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid “overfitting” to recent highs; if last 3 days are >65.0, cap forecast at +5% above 30-day moving average.
